circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has been the home of Formula One's season finale since 2009 and was designed by Hermann Tilke. The venue represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit, following Bahrain and preceding installations in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting motorsport events. As a Grade 1 FIA-licensed facility, it serves as one of the championship's traditional opening rounds and attracts various racing series to compete on its layout.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit has a storied history hosting the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct periods: initially as the Österreichring from 1970 to 1987, then following restructuring and renaming as the A1-Ring from 1997 to 2003. The track underwent modifications including a shortening and rebuilding between these hosting eras.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, spanning 6. 003 km to rank as the fourth-longest venue on the Formula One calendar. The circuit first hosted Formula One racing in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the inaugural Middle Eastern Formula One Grand Prix that year. Beyond its annual Formula One fixture, the venue accommodates various racing categories including GP2 Series competition and 24-hour endurance events, while Australian V8 Supercars competed there from 2006 until 2010.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced combination of lengthy straightaways and diverse corner configurations that test multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has been hosting Grand Prix racing since 1925 and featured prominently in Formula One's inaugural 1950 season. The venue has served as the home of the Belgian Grand Prix consistently from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, this 4. 361 km racing circuit serves as the home of the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond hosting the premier motorsport event, the venue has accommodated various other international racing series including sports car championships and North American touring car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit is a Chinese motorsport venue located in Shanghai's Jiading District that gained prominence as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which took place there from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. In addition to hosting Formula One racing, the facility began featuring electric racing events from 2024 onward.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Northamptonshire in England, Silverstone Circuit has been the primary venue for Britain's Formula One Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After rotating among three British circuits during the 1955-1986 period, the Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km track that hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc in 1986. Built in just eight months near a major highway after the government rejected plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park, the venue was established as a memorial to János Drapál, a pioneering Hungarian motorcycle racer.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza, located near Milan in northern Italy, is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility. The venue has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, except for a 1980 closure for upgrades, and earns its nickname "the Temple of Speed" from its lengthy straightaways and rapid cornering sections.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue located in Mie Prefecture and operated by Honda Mobilityland. The track hosts major international racing championships, most notably Formula One and Super Formula competitions, with a spectator capacity of 155,000.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, weaving around the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding entertainment venues. The 3. 8-mile layout incorporates iconic landmarks such as the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a unique urban racing environment in the heart of the casino district.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez takes its name from two brothers who died in racing accidents in the 1960s. The circuit resumed hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in 2015 after a 23-year absence, featuring a revised layout compared to its previous configurations used through 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that debuted on the Formula One calendar in 2022. The 3. 363-mile layout comprises 19 corners and produces qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph, designed specifically by specialized circuit engineers for the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco winds through the Monte Carlo district of the Principality, measuring 3. 337 kilometres and following the urban streets around Monaco's harbour. The venue is widely known as Monte Carlo, reflecting the location of most of its layout within that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the Zandvoort circuit measures 4. 259 kilometers and hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after returning to Formula One in 2021 following a lengthy absence. The track's involvement in the championship concludes in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419 km track featuring a 1. 068 km main straight and holds FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian motorsport venue in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal 1977 plane crash. The counterclockwise circuit includes a kart facility dedicated to Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Jeddah's waterfront beside the Red Sea. Since its inauguration in 2021, it has served as the home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, with the circuit expanding to include Formula E racing from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Downtown Core and Kallang districts, forming a temporary racing layout that circles the Marina Bay waterfront.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometer Spanish racing facility features a balanced combination of extended straights and varied corner configurations, making it versatile for testing different racing skills. The track holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the venue hosts major motorsport events including NASCAR, MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas, and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, while previously accommodating various other racing series.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British racing driver who represents Thailand in Formula One, currently driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 alongside 32 Grand Prix victories across his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including World Endurance Championship glory in 2018-19 and two Le Mans 24 Hours victories with Toyota, making him the sole driver to win both Formula One and World Endurance world titles.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One debut in 2025 and currently races for Mercedes, where he has claimed six Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team. His full name is Gabriel Lourenzo Bortoleto Oliveira.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas competes for Cadillac in Formula One, having secured two runner-up championship finishes during his time with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020. Across his 13-season career, he has claimed victories in 10 Grand Prix events.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races in Formula One for the Alpine team. He represents his nation in one of motorsport's premier competitions.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian driver competing in European endurance racing with Nielsen Racing while holding a reserve role at Haas in Formula One, where he has participated in seven races during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French driver Pierre Gasly currently races for Alpine in Formula One, having previously achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, a driver with French and Algerian heritage, currently races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One while competing under the French flag.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding an unprecedented seven world championship titles that he shares with Michael Schumacher. His career achievements include the most race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he has achieved notable success in endurance motorsport, including victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a racing driver from Monaco, currently drives for Ferrari in Formula One. He finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver known as K-Mag, raced in Formula One across two separate periods spanning 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. Currently, he competes as a factory driver for BMW in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT, while also pursuing a part-time career in NASCAR's top series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris represents Great Britain in Formula One racing for McLaren, where he secured the world championship title in 2025. The driver has claimed 12 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The driver achieved a Grand Prix victory in 2021 at the Hungarian round while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his 15-year career in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull Racing.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver currently competing for McLaren in Formula One, has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-season tenure in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo is an Australian driver who competed in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, earning the nickname "the Honey Badger" during his 14-season career. He achieved eight Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell is a British Formula One driver competing for Mercedes who has achieved seven race victories over his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories over his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant participated in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following his prior involvement in the IMSA LMP2 class with Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently competing for Aston Martin in the championship series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda held a Formula One seat from 2021 through 2025 and currently functions as a reserve driver for both Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch driver Max Verstappen has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024 while racing for Red Bull Racing, accumulating 71 Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China in motorsport as a reserve driver for Cadillac's Formula One operation. The racing driver competed in the premier series from 2022 through 2024 and holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese competitor to have raced in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing operates from Enstone as Renault's works team under French racing credentials, having been rebranded from Renault F1 Team in 2021 to showcase the Alpine sports car brand. The squad secured its only victory during this era when Esteban Ocon triumphed at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, and currently competes with Mercedes powerplants while fielding Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has appeared in Formula One through different incarnations, with its current iteration competing as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team under AMR GP Limited.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari HP represents the motorsport arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari and stands as both the longest-continuously competing and most accomplished team in Formula One history, participating in every World Championship since the sport's inaugural season in 1950. The squad carries the legendary "Prancing Horse" moniker derived from their iconic emblem.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: American entrepreneur Gene Haas founded this Formula One team in 2014, with the squad making its competitive debut in 2016. The team changed leadership in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu took over as principal, succeeding the founding team principal who held the position since the team's establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss constructor founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, the team established itself through endurance racing success including the 1989 Le Mans victory before competing in Formula One from 1993 onward. The operation underwent various transformations throughout its F1 tenure before concluding in 2025 as the fourth-longest-serving constructor by race entries, with Audi acquiring the team and its infrastructure in 2024 to establish its own F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its technology facility in Woking that competes as McLaren Mastercard F1 Team. Operating as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group, the team is owned by Bahrain's Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the current works team based in Brackley and operating under a German licence. Since 2022, the team has been jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff in equal thirds. The marque's racing programmes are traditionally associated with the "Silver Arrows" nomenclature.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024, operating as Red Bull GmbH's second team alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the outfit serves as part of the Austrian conglomerate's dual-team Formula One structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024, operating as one of two teams under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team functions as a sister operation within the Red Bull Formula One programme.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team operating from England and owned by Red Bull GmbH alongside Racing Bulls. Founded in 2005 and led by Christian Horner until his 2025 departure, the team is now under Laurent Mekies's management.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, stands as a prominent British Formula One constructor based in Grove, Oxfordshire. Founded following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture, the team has evolved into a major player in the sport's competitive landscape.
